rccg_open_heavens.title: REMAIN GRATEFUL
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works.
message: Sometime ago, I went to a man's house to conduct a programme. It was a night programme, and the owner of the house asked me to spend the night at his house afterwards because it was too late for me to return home. I obliged, and in the morning, he asked me to wait for breakfast. When it was time to eat, a chef came and asked my host what he wanted to eat. After so much back and forth, my host finally decided that he would have bread and eggs for breakfast. Then, for the next few minutes, another back-and-forth ensued because the chef asked my host how he wanted his eggs prepared - scrambled, poached, or fried - before he finally settled on boiled eggs. Then, it was time for another debate: how do you want your egg boiled, hard-boiled or medium-boiled? By then, it had been more than 25 minutes, and I had gotten really hungry. Finally, the chef turned to me when he finished with his boss and asked, "Sir, what will you eat?" I told him to give me anything he had. He said he had bread and eggs, and I said it was fine. Then, he asked if I wanted an omelette or bacon, the number of eggs I wanted, and so on. I told him that anything was fine, as long as it was enough to satisfy my hunger. After the whole ordeal, I thought to myself that even though I had no money, I had a good appetite at least. Child of God, while you may not have everything you desire in life yet, you must be grateful for the things you have.

Ecclesiastes 6:9 says that the sight of the eyes is better than the wandering of desire. Many people are not grateful for what they have because they are consumed with thinking about the things they want. They do not appreciate the things they can see because of their wandering desires. Beloved, if God has given you the gift of life, be grateful. Ecclesiastes 9:4 says that as long as you are joined to all the living, there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion. As long as you are alive, there is hope that you will achieve the things you desire. Don't be so focused on the things you wish you had that you forget to appreciate God for all you already have. In all things, give thanks (1 Thessalonians 5:18).
prayerPoints: Reflection:  Are you grateful for the things you have?

mfm_mfm.title: Pray For Your Country
mfm_mfm.author: Dr. D.K. Olukoya
mfm_mfm.memoryVerseText: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
message: the inhabitants thereof for His purpose and glory. All the glorious plans of God for every nation can only become a reality as the nations and her citizens submit to the will of God and exalt righteous living above vicious existence. That is the reason why the Scripture says, “Righteousness exalts a nation but sin is a reproach to any people” (Proverbs 14:34),

However, the devil has been instigating the nations of the world against the plan, the purpose and the will of God for them, thereby derailing divine agenda for them and also setting them up for divine punishment. The judgement of God came upon Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24-25). Several other nations and even Israel were judged by God because of their wickedness and iniquitous living. God’s judgement was also declared upon Bethsaida, Chorazin, and Capernaum because of their stiff-neckedness (Matthew 11:20-24). Another sad reality is the fact that there are dark spiritual princes instituted as commanders and evil influencers over nations like the Prince of Persia in Daniel chapter ten. All these forces combine to truncate the beautiful plans of God for nations, bringing them into bondage, confusion, systemic failure, poverty, political and socio-economic crises of different degrees, famine, wars and other critical conditions.

It is because of all these wicked attacks that God counsels His people to always pray for the peace of their nation as we have read in today’s Fire Scripture. You too must pray for the peace and prosperity of your nation. Pray for political stability and economic growth. Pray for all the leaders that God will give them the wisdom and courage to always follow the right path. Ask God to heal your nation and restore her glory. Pray that the will of God be established over every sector of your nation and over every household. And pray that the gospel of Jesus Christ will prevail over your nation.

dclm_dclm.title: Avoid Costly Mistakes
dclm_dclm.author: Pastor W.F. Kumuyi
dclm_dclm.memoryVerseText: Therefore, O Aholibah, thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will raise up thy lovers against thee, from whom thy mind is alienated, and I will bring them against thee on every side
message: Many times, what gets people into trouble are not big but little things. They omit to do what is right. They indulge in little careless or reckless acts, including those they knew spelt disaster for other people. With the passage of time, they become self confident in their ability to tackle issues their own way. They dismiss pointers in their own lives to things that caused misfortune for others on the hollow belief that ‘it cannot happen to me’. In the process, they seal their own misfortune.

Aholibah, or Judah in Israel, had witnessed judgement that came on Samaria (or Aholah) for turning away from God and embracing the nations that did not know the Lord. They were shipped into exile. Instead of learning from God’s retribution on evil nations, Judah became more sinful before God. They connived, formed alliances with heathen nations, exposed their treasure to them and served their idols. God paid them in their own coins: He turned their new friends against them, who plundered their wealth and exposed them to shame, humiliation and disgrace.

It is only reasonable to learn from the mistakes of other people and avoid things that brought them down. Where we find that the pursuit of power, wealth and pleasure took them away from God, we must flee from such. The lives of those around us who fell out with God should be a lesson to us to shun their ways. Anything that will lull our minds and dull our sensitivity to sinful enjoyment must be avoided. We must not wait to taste the judgment of God. Anything we must do to live right before God and avoid His rod of punishment must be done now. Mercifully, God gives us grace to live the acceptable life before Him. It is thus up to us to fully tap into that inexhaustible grace and present a commendable portrait of glory and beauty, rooted in His love.
dclm_dclm.thoughtForTheDay: Sin is deceptive and deadly, and those that toy with it have bitter tales to tell.

rccg_rccg_ss_adult.assignments: List five (5) practical ways a believer can daily live a sanctified life (2×5=10 marks).
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.introduction: Sanctification is a spiritual surgery performed by God in the life of a saved soul (Ezekiel 36:26). It is the second work of grace after salvation. Sanctification simply means to make holy, pure and separated unto God (Jeremiah 1:4-5). It is a progressive work of God in man that makes us free from sin and be like Christ (1 Thessalonians 5:23; Romans 8:13). It is vital to understand the process and benefits of sanctification.
outlines: THE PROCESS
THE BENEFITS
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.discussion:
1. THE PROCESS

A. To be sanctified

You need to see yourself as you are: filthy and in need of help
Cry to God for deliverance (Isaiah 6:5).
Present yourself to the Sanctifier – God (1 Thessalonians 5:23).
Surrender your heart to the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:2; 2 Thessalonians 2:13).
Study the word of God (John 17:17).
Soak yourself in the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 9:13-14; 1 John 1:7, 9).
Daily surrender to God (Colossians 3:6-10; Romans 6:13).
B. This process can be a painful experience, but:

The result is that you are broken and transformed into a new nature (Galatians 2:20; 2 Timothy 2:3-4).
The awareness that you do not own yourself anymore helps you prioritise God in everything you do, and whatever does not glorify Him is a no-go area for you (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
CLASS ACTIVITY 1: How do we avoid things that defile His Temple?

2. THE BENEFITS

Sanctification represents a believer’s victory over the flesh (Romans 7:24-25), the world (1 John 5:4), and the devil (James 4:7).
A sanctified believer will enjoy the ability to easily resist temptation because there is a renewed hatred for sin and lust.
Sanctification fosters intimacy with God, increases spiritual strength and stability (Psalm 15:1-5).
It also aids a ‘clean record’ for believers, that is, the enemy will not have to fool God over such (John 14:30).
It helps believers to be humble and submissive to God and to constituted authorities. The Adamic nature in man is subdued (Romans 8:1-5).
It gives the believer control over self (Galatians 2:20; Romans 6:13).
It promotes right standing before God and pure intentions of actions and words (Acts 24:16).
CLASS ACTIVITY 2: The class should discuss the ways sanctification helps a believer to live a life that honours God.
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.summary:
CONCLUSION: Sanctification is an integral part of Christian growth; every child of God must earnestly desire it.

EVALUATION: Briefly explain the process of sanctification.

CLOSING PRAYER: Father, I receive the grace to continually yield myself to your sanctification process in Jesus’ name.

christ_embassy_rhapsody.title: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
christ_embassy_rhapsody.author: Pastor Chris Oyakhilome
christ_embassy_rhapsody.topic: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
christ_embassy_rhapsody.memoryVerseText: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…
message: 1 Peter 1:23 tells us something remarkable; it says, “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” A similar truth is emphasized in James 1:18, “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” God’s Word gave birth to you; and what does that make you?

It means you’re the Word in flesh! The Word of God is your life-source, and every living thing must be connected to its source to live. This is why your fellowship with the Word is so important. Your true life and environment are in the Word. If you live outside the Word, you’re functioning outside your divine environment.

The Apostle Paul, by the Spirit, connects and unveils this beautifully in 2 Corinthians 3:2-3. First, he says, “Ye are our epistle…” and then he goes further to say, “…ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…” You’re the living epistle, the living message, the living expression of Christ to your world. The Lord Jesus is called the living Word; therefore, being born of His Word, you carry His life, nature, wisdom and character within you.

You’re indestructible because you’re born of His indestructible seed (His Word), which lives and abides forever. Therefore, your sufficiency, your ability, competence, strength and capacity come from your divine origin. Many struggle in life because they don’t live according to this truth. They attempt to live outside the environment of the Word.

But the Christian who meditates on the Word continually stays connected to the source of his divine nature. The more the Word dominates your spirit, the more your true nature is unveiled. God’s Word created the universe. His Word is everything. As you meditate on it, it transforms your life. Think, speak, and live the Word. Glory to God!

odm_odm.title: Our Daily Manna
odm_odm.author: Bishop Dr. Chris Kwakpovwe
odm_odm.memoryVerseText: When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.
odm_odm.devotionalCapsule: When God is ready to perform His wonders, protocols are suspended and mockers are silenced!
message: Beloved, our God is never late! Even when the clock of life appears to have ticked to the final second and your adversaries have already written your spiritual obituary, Jehovah El-Shaddai steps into the arena and reverses the irreversible! (Psalm 126:1).
Don't lose your joy because of temporary setbacks or stubborn delays. Delay is never denial in God's kingdom agenda. Hold on to your faith!
God is setting an ambush against your adversaries, and your mockers shall soon gather to congratulate you!
prayerPoints: O God of eleventh-hour miracles, arise and turn my captivity around this month, in Jesus' name.
Every power assigned to prolong my struggle, expire by fire, in the name of Jesus.

dunamis_seeds.title: The Practice Of Love
dunamis_seeds.author: Pastor Dr. Paul Enenche
dunamis_seeds.memoryVerseText: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal… Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil.
message: Our anchor Scripture emphasizes the importance of love above all other virtues. It makes four things critically clear:

1.	Speaking in tongues equals noise without love. Lovelessness drowns the voice of prayer. Hatred or unforgiveness in the heart drowns a person’s voice at the place of prayer. If you do not love your brother, sister, or neighbour, you are wasting your time at the place of prayer.

2.	Insight from Scripture is a waste without love. Revelation cannot guarantee any meaningful outcome in the absence of love. Where love is absent, revelation means nothing; insight means nothing. That is why there are many people whose heads are filled with Scripture, but their lives are empty of results. It doesn’t matter what you know; until you know love, you know nothing.

3.	Faith is fake without love, because faith worketh by love (Galatians 5:6). Many people say, “I believe, I have faith,” while there is bitterness in their heart towards someone, and still wonder why they are not seeing results.

4.	Giving is unprofitable without love. Even giving one’s body to be burned for the sake of the gospel profits nothing without love.
Giving without love equals sowing without reaping; such giving is not permitted to yield the expected harvest. 1 Corinthians 13:3If prayer is useless without love, if revelation is a waste without love, if faith cannot work without love, and if sowing is useless without love, then nothing we do is meaningful and profitable without love.
Now, what is the practicality of love? We shall be looking at a few of them in our study today.

1.	Love is very patient (1 Corinthians 13:4).
Love is both tolerant and tireless. It has a large capacity to accommodate human error. Living with a spouse requires this kind of patience

2.	Love is kind (1 Corinthians 13:4).
Love is liberal; love is not tight-fisted or stingy. A man who is tight-fisted toward his wife, children, and other loved ones is operating outside the vocabulary of love.

3.	Love does not envy (1 Corinthians 13:4).
When you love people, you don’t compete with them; you commend their effort. Love does not struggle to outdo, undo, or diminish others; it struggles only to give honest expression to what God has placed within, not to create impressions.
Beloved, love is life. Walk in love, because love affects life, both in time and in eternity. Love guarantees profitability and productivity for our spirituality. Our prayer life, giving, faith, and insight are all at the mercy of our love walk.
prayerPoints: Father, let love be the foundation of everything I do, so that none of my effort is wasted. Teach me to be patient, kind, and give me the grace to make amends where necessary, Lord, in Jesus’ Name.
dunamis_seeds.thoughtForTheDay: It doesn’t matter what you know; until you know love, you know nothing.

rccg_rccg_yaya_student.introduction: Sanctification is a spiritual surgery performed by God in the life of a saved soul (Ezekiel 36:26). It is the second work of grace after salvation. Sanctification simply means to make holy, pure and separated unto God (Jeremiah 1:4-5). It is a progressive work of God in man that makes us free from sin and be like Christ (1 Thessalonians 5:23; Romans 8:13). It is vital to understand the process and benefits of sanctification.
outlines: THE PROCESS
THE BENEFITS
rccg_rccg_yaya_student.discussion:
1. THE PROCESS

A. To be sanctified

You need to see yourself as you are: filthy and in need of help
Cry to God for deliverance (Isaiah 6:5).
Present yourself to the Sanctifier – God (1 Thessalonians 5:23).
Surrender your heart to the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:2; 2 Thessalonians 2:13).
Study the word of God (John 17:17).
Soak yourself in the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 9:13-14; 1 John 1:7, 9).
Daily surrender to God (Colossians 3:6-10; Romans 6:13).
B. This process can be a painful experience, but:

The result is that you are broken and transformed into a new nature (Galatians 2:20; 2 Timothy 2:3-4).
The awareness that you do not own yourself anymore helps you prioritise God in everything you do, and whatever does not glorify Him is a no-go area for you (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
CLASS ACTIVITY 1: How do we avoid things that defile His Temple?

2. THE BENEFITS

Sanctification represents a believer’s victory over the flesh (Romans 7:24-25), the world (1 John 5:4), and the devil (James 4:7).
A sanctified believer will enjoy the ability to easily resist temptation because there is a renewed hatred for sin and lust.
Sanctification fosters intimacy with God, increases spiritual strength and stability (Psalm 15:1-5).
It also aids a ‘clean record’ for believers, that is, the enemy will not have to fool God over such (John 14:30).
It helps believers to be humble and submissive to God and to constituted authorities. The Adamic nature in man is subdued (Romans 8:1-5).
It gives the believer control over self (Galatians 2:20; Romans 6:13).
It promotes right standing before God and pure intentions of actions and words (Acts 24:16).
CLASS ACTIVITY 2: The class should discuss the ways sanctification helps a believer to live a life that honours God.

CONCLUSION: Sanctification is an integral part of Christian growth; every child of God must earnestly desire it.

EVALUATION: Briefly explain the process of sanctification.

CLOSING PRAYER: Father, I receive the grace to continually yield myself to your sanctification process in Jesus’ name.

rhapsody.title: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
rhapsody.author: Pastor Chris Oyakhilome
rhapsody.topic: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
rhapsody.memoryVerseText: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…
message: 1 Peter 1:23 tells us something remarkable; it says, “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” A similar truth is emphasized in James 1:18, “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” God’s Word gave birth to you; and what does that make you?

It means you’re the Word in flesh! The Word of God is your life-source, and every living thing must be connected to its source to live. This is why your fellowship with the Word is so important. Your true life and environment are in the Word. If you live outside the Word, you’re functioning outside your divine environment.

The Apostle Paul, by the Spirit, connects and unveils this beautifully in 2 Corinthians 3:2-3. First, he says, “Ye are our epistle…” and then he goes further to say, “…ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…” You’re the living epistle, the living message, the living expression of Christ to your world. The Lord Jesus is called the living Word; therefore, being born of His Word, you carry His life, nature, wisdom and character within you.

You’re indestructible because you’re born of His indestructible seed (His Word), which lives and abides forever. Therefore, your sufficiency, your ability, competence, strength and capacity come from your divine origin. Many struggle in life because they don’t live according to this truth. They attempt to live outside the environment of the Word.

But the Christian who meditates on the Word continually stays connected to the source of his divine nature. The more the Word dominates your spirit, the more your true nature is unveiled. God’s Word created the universe. His Word is everything. As you meditate on it, it transforms your life. Think, speak, and live the Word. Glory to God!
rhapsody.hymn: I’m born of God’s incorruptible Word; I’m the living epistle of Christ. My life is the manifestation of divine wisdom, glory and power. As I meditate on the Word, even now, I’m strengthened, transformed and established in victory, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

open_heavens.title: REMAIN GRATEFUL
open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
open_heavens.memoryVerseText: That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works.
message: Sometime ago, I went to a man's house to conduct a programme. It was a night programme, and the owner of the house asked me to spend the night at his house afterwards because it was too late for me to return home. I obliged, and in the morning, he asked me to wait for breakfast. When it was time to eat, a chef came and asked my host what he wanted to eat. After so much back and forth, my host finally decided that he would have bread and eggs for breakfast. Then, for the next few minutes, another back-and-forth ensued because the chef asked my host how he wanted his eggs prepared - scrambled, poached, or fried - before he finally settled on boiled eggs. Then, it was time for another debate: how do you want your egg boiled, hard-boiled or medium-boiled? By then, it had been more than 25 minutes, and I had gotten really hungry. Finally, the chef turned to me when he finished with his boss and asked, "Sir, what will you eat?" I told him to give me anything he had. He said he had bread and eggs, and I said it was fine. Then, he asked if I wanted an omelette or bacon, the number of eggs I wanted, and so on. I told him that anything was fine, as long as it was enough to satisfy my hunger. After the whole ordeal, I thought to myself that even though I had no money, I had a good appetite at least. Child of God, while you may not have everything you desire in life yet, you must be grateful for the things you have.

Ecclesiastes 6:9 says that the sight of the eyes is better than the wandering of desire. Many people are not grateful for what they have because they are consumed with thinking about the things they want. They do not appreciate the things they can see because of their wandering desires. Beloved, if God has given you the gift of life, be grateful. Ecclesiastes 9:4 says that as long as you are joined to all the living, there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion. As long as you are alive, there is hope that you will achieve the things you desire. Don't be so focused on the things you wish you had that you forget to appreciate God for all you already have. In all things, give thanks (1 Thessalonians 5:18).
prayerPoints: Reflection:  Are you grateful for the things you have?
open_heavens.hymn: Praise To The Lord The Almighty, The King Of Creation

mfm.title: Pray For Your Country
mfm.author: Dr. D.K. Olukoya
mfm.memoryVerseText: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
message: the inhabitants thereof for His purpose and glory. All the glorious plans of God for every nation can only become a reality as the nations and her citizens submit to the will of God and exalt righteous living above vicious existence. That is the reason why the Scripture says, “Righteousness exalts a nation but sin is a reproach to any people” (Proverbs 14:34),

However, the devil has been instigating the nations of the world against the plan, the purpose and the will of God for them, thereby derailing divine agenda for them and also setting them up for divine punishment. The judgement of God came upon Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24-25). Several other nations and even Israel were judged by God because of their wickedness and iniquitous living. God’s judgement was also declared upon Bethsaida, Chorazin, and Capernaum because of their stiff-neckedness (Matthew 11:20-24). Another sad reality is the fact that there are dark spiritual princes instituted as commanders and evil influencers over nations like the Prince of Persia in Daniel chapter ten. All these forces combine to truncate the beautiful plans of God for nations, bringing them into bondage, confusion, systemic failure, poverty, political and socio-economic crises of different degrees, famine, wars and other critical conditions.

It is because of all these wicked attacks that God counsels His people to always pray for the peace of their nation as we have read in today’s Fire Scripture. You too must pray for the peace and prosperity of your nation. Pray for political stability and economic growth. Pray for all the leaders that God will give them the wisdom and courage to always follow the right path. Ask God to heal your nation and restore her glory. Pray that the will of God be established over every sector of your nation and over every household. And pray that the gospel of Jesus Christ will prevail over your nation.
mfm.motivationalQuote: Praying for your nation is a means of realignment with divine purpose.
mfm.propheticWord: I decree that your nation shall continue to experience God’s favour, in the Name of Jesus.
mfm.propheticDeclaration: I decree that your nation shall continue to experience God’s favour, in the Name of Jesus.

seeds.title: The Practice Of Love
seeds.author: Pastor Dr. Paul Enenche
seeds.memoryVerseText: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal… Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil.
message: Our anchor Scripture emphasizes the importance of love above all other virtues. It makes four things critically clear:

1.	Speaking in tongues equals noise without love. Lovelessness drowns the voice of prayer. Hatred or unforgiveness in the heart drowns a person’s voice at the place of prayer. If you do not love your brother, sister, or neighbour, you are wasting your time at the place of prayer.

2.	Insight from Scripture is a waste without love. Revelation cannot guarantee any meaningful outcome in the absence of love. Where love is absent, revelation means nothing; insight means nothing. That is why there are many people whose heads are filled with Scripture, but their lives are empty of results. It doesn’t matter what you know; until you know love, you know nothing.

3.	Faith is fake without love, because faith worketh by love (Galatians 5:6). Many people say, “I believe, I have faith,” while there is bitterness in their heart towards someone, and still wonder why they are not seeing results.

4.	Giving is unprofitable without love. Even giving one’s body to be burned for the sake of the gospel profits nothing without love.
Giving without love equals sowing without reaping; such giving is not permitted to yield the expected harvest. 1 Corinthians 13:3If prayer is useless without love, if revelation is a waste without love, if faith cannot work without love, and if sowing is useless without love, then nothing we do is meaningful and profitable without love.
Now, what is the practicality of love? We shall be looking at a few of them in our study today.

1.	Love is very patient (1 Corinthians 13:4).
Love is both tolerant and tireless. It has a large capacity to accommodate human error. Living with a spouse requires this kind of patience

2.	Love is kind (1 Corinthians 13:4).
Love is liberal; love is not tight-fisted or stingy. A man who is tight-fisted toward his wife, children, and other loved ones is operating outside the vocabulary of love.

3.	Love does not envy (1 Corinthians 13:4).
When you love people, you don’t compete with them; you commend their effort. Love does not struggle to outdo, undo, or diminish others; it struggles only to give honest expression to what God has placed within, not to create impressions.
Beloved, love is life. Walk in love, because love affects life, both in time and in eternity. Love guarantees profitability and productivity for our spirituality. Our prayer life, giving, faith, and insight are all at the mercy of our love walk.
prayerPoints: Father, let love be the foundation of everything I do, so that none of my effort is wasted. Teach me to be patient, kind, and give me the grace to make amends where necessary, Lord, in Jesus’ Name.
seeds.thoughtForTheDay: It doesn’t matter what you know; until you know love, you know nothing.

3.	Faith is fake without love, because faith worketh by love (Galatians 5:6). Many people say, “I believe, I have faith,” while there is bitterness in their heart towards someone, and still wonder why they are not seeing results.

4.	Giving is unprofitable without love. Even giving one’s body to be burned for the sake of the gospel profits nothing without love.
Giving without love equals sowing without reaping; such giving is not permitted to yield the expected harvest. 1 Corinthians 13:3If prayer is useless without love, if revelation is a waste without love, if faith cannot work without love, and if sowing is useless without love, then nothing we do is meaningful and profitable without love.
Now, what is the practicality of love? We shall be looking at a few of them in our study today.

1.	Love is very patient (1 Corinthians 13:4).
Love is both tolerant and tireless. It has a large capacity to accommodate human error. Living with a spouse requires this kind of patience

2.	Love is kind (1 Corinthians 13:4).
Love is liberal; love is not tight-fisted or stingy. A man who is tight-fisted toward his wife, children, and other loved ones is operating outside the vocabulary of love.

3.	Love does not envy (1 Corinthians 13:4).
When you love people, you don’t compete with them; you commend their effort. Love does not struggle to outdo, undo, or diminish others; it struggles only to give honest expression to what God has placed within, not to create impressions.
Beloved, love is life. Walk in love, because love affects life, both in time and in eternity. Love guarantees profitability and productivity for our spirituality. Our prayer life, giving, faith, and insight are all at the mercy of our love walk.
prayerPoints: Father, let love be the foundation of everything I do, so that none of my effort is wasted. Teach me to be patient, kind, and give me the grace to make amends where necessary, Lord, in Jesus’ Name.

rccg_open_heavens.title: More Than a Conqueror
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.
message: Life is full of battles. From the moment we are born until we leave this world, we experience different challenges. However, when a person comes to Christ, everything changes. Through Christ, the believer becomes a new creation, and the battles of life no longer have to determine the outcome. Instead of struggling without hope of victory, the believer can live with the assurance of victory in Christ.

Romans 8:37 tells believers that they are more than conquerors through Christ. A conqueror fights and defeats an enemy to obtain victory, while someone who is more than a conqueror enjoys a victory that has already been achieved. As believers, we are recipients of the victory Jesus has won.

Jesus went to the cross, defeated the devil, and secured victory for humanity. After His resurrection, He declared that all authority in heaven and on earth had been given to Him (Matthew 28:18). He then gave power to His disciples through the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:8).

When the disciples received the Holy Spirit, they began to operate in the authority Christ had given them. They cast out demons, healed the sick, preached the gospel, and continued to spread the message of Christ even when they encountered persecution. When persecution caused believers to scatter, they used the opportunity to preach the gospel in other places (Acts 8:1–4). Philip, for example, went to Samaria, where many people received the message and the city experienced great spiritual impact (Acts 8:5–8).

Being more than a conqueror does not mean that you will never face challenges. Rather, it means that when challenges arise, you can face them with the confidence that God can work through them for His purpose. What appears to be an attack can ultimately become an opportunity for God to accomplish His plan.

The death of Jesus on the cross is a powerful example. The enemy intended the crucifixion for destruction, but God used it to accomplish salvation. 1 Corinthians 2:8 explains that the rulers of that age did not understand the wisdom of God in what was taking place.
Therefore, remain confident in Christ. Trust God even when circumstances appear difficult, knowing that He can turn situations around and cause His purpose to prevail.
prayerPoints: Key Point: Being more than a conqueror means that you will always triumph over the enemy's plans.
rccg_open_heavens.hymn: Conquerors and Overcomers Now Are We

rccg_open_heavens.title: WEEP NOT
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness.
message: Sometime ago, I was praying during a programme and God said, "Open your eyes." I was almost going to say, "Lord, but I'm praying"; however, I obeyed. As I opened my eyes, I saw a woman in the congregation, her face soaked in tears, weeping as she prayed. Then, God said, "Go and tell her, 'Weep not.'" I moved towards the congregation, approached her, and tapped her as I said, "God said, 'Weep not.'" Her eyes brightened, and I returned to the altar to continue praying. A year later, that same woman stood before me, along with some other people who wanted me to pray for them. When it was her turn for me to pray for her, I greeted her and said, "Sister, how can I help you?" She opened her mouth and could only mutter, "Jesus". I asked her a second time how I could help her, and she only said, "Jesus" again. I asked her a third time, and she said the same thing. I began to get impatient because there were other people in the queue. Eventually, she got herself together, and she told me that she was the woman whom God sent me to tell not to weep the previous year. She then told me that she was crying that day because she had been married for over ten years without any children, and her husband's relatives were urging him to send her packing if she didn't give birth to any children soon. As she shared her story, I immediately understood why she found it difficult to speak at first; she was holding a baby in her right hand and another in her left. God turned her seemingly hopeless situation into an occasion for rejoicing. I pray that God will turn any seemingly hopeless situation that might exist in your life around and fill your mouth with laughter, in Jesus' name.

Beloved, if you have surrendered your life to the Lord Jesus Christ, my Daddy is saying to you today, "Weep not," just like Jesus said to the widow of Nain in today's Bible reading. Every time Jesus says, "Weep not," it is because He wants to perform a miracle. No matter how long you may have been weeping, your time of rejoicing has come. Weeping may endure for a night, but joy will surely come in the morning (Psalm 30:5). I decree that your days of rejoicing are here, in Jesus' name.
prayerPoints: Father, thank You for putting an end to my weeping and for bringing me into my days of rejoicing.
rccg_open_heavens.hymn: What A Friend We Have In Jesus

rccg_open_heavens.title: GOD OF HOPE
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
message: After Jesus died, His disciples became afraid and lost hope. John 21:3 tells us that Peter said to the other disciples, "I go a fishing." He wasn't going to fish for souls; instead, he was returning to his old job because he had lost hope. He must have thought to himself, "We thought Jesus Christ was going to rescue us from all those who are oppressing us. We thought that the age of miracles had come to stay, but now He has been crucified on a cross." When Peter told the other disciples that he was going fishing, they joined him because they had also lost hope. They felt that the best thing they could do was to return to fishing. However, Jesus appeared to them that morning as they fished and restored their hope. As they struggled to catch fish, Jesus called out to them and showed them where to cast their net. He turned their hopelessness into joy. I declare that God will show up for you and turn every hopeless situation you may be experiencing around, in Jesus' name.

Child of God, when all hope is lost and people have given up on you, do not give up on yourself. If, peradventure, you have given up on yourself, do not give up on God because He will always show up for the hopeless when they turn to Him. Today's memory verse calls Him 'the God of hope'

Some years ago, a young man was travelling from Kaduna, a state in Northern Nigeria, to Lagos with some other people in a vehicle. While they were on their way, they had an accident and everyone in the vehicle died except the young man. He was taken to a hospital because he was still breathing, even though he was unconscious. He was in a coma for several days, and every once in a while, he would wake up and shout, "Jesus," before returning to the coma. After a while, the doctors concluded that his case was hopeless, but they couldn't bury him because he was still breathing. Then one day, he awoke, cried out 'Jesus!', opened his eyes, and never slipped back into the coma. That young man is still alive today.

Beloved, I pray that if there is any situation in your life that people around you have concluded to be hopeless, you will receive a new lease of life from the Almighty that will transform it into a testimony, in Jesus' name.
prayerPoints: Key Point: The Almighty God is a God of hope; therefore, you must never lose hope.
rccg_open_heavens.hymn: 'Tis So Sweet To Trust In Jesus

rccg_open_heavens.title: HE SPEAKS PEACE
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: I will hear what God the LORD will speak: for he will speak peace unto his people, and to his saints: but let them not turn again to folly.
message: After Jesus resurrected from the dead, He entered the room where His disciples had gathered because they were afraid and immediately told them, "Peace be unto you" (John 20:19). In John 14:27, Jesus also said:
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

Jesus gives His followers peace because He is the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6). In Mark 4:35-41, the Bible tells us that Jesus and His disciples were in a ship, and a massive storm arose. While they were scared for their lives and were trying so hard to manage the situation, Jesus was sleeping peacefully. The moment they woke Him up, He issued only one decree, "Peace, be still," and everything became calm. In the name above every other name, I decree that the peace of God that passes all understanding will rest upon you at all times, in Jesus' name.

Today's memory verse tells us that God speaks peace to His people. It is important to understand that God is never the author of confusion or chaos (1 Corinthians 14:33). Whenever you sense confusion or chaos around you, know that the devil is at work because James 3:14-16 says that where envying and strife are present (which are earthly, sensual, and devilish), there is confusion and every evil work. When the earth was in a state of chaos and darkness covered the face of the deep in Genesis 1:2, God's word brought order to the situation.

Beloved, whenever you are in a state of confusion and chaos, cry out to God for help and listen to what He has to say to you. His Word will always bring peace and show you the way out of the situation. To receive the peace that the Prince of Peace gives, however, you must surrender your life to Him. People who insist on living on their own terms will not enjoy the peace of the Lord because His peace thrives only where His way is followed, and His will is done.

God wants to speak peace into any troubled water that might exist in your life. To enjoy His peace, however, you must never insist on calming any storm you may be facing your own way. Surrender to God totally, and His peace shall rule every facet of your life.
prayerPoints: Key Point: God's peace rules where His way is followed and His will is done.

rccg_open_heavens.title: HE SPEAKS PEACE II
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
message: Storms can come in various forms and with varying degrees of intensity. I recall an incident some years ago, when I was travelling from Lagos to London on a plane. When we were about to land at Heathrow Airport, the captain informed us that there was a problem with the door at the belly of the aircraft, and we all understood it to mean that the landing gear wouldn't be able to function, and in essence, the pilot was going to have to crash-land the plane. There was a storm on the plane at that moment because confusion and pandemonium broke out all around me. That day, I discovered that rich people do not want to die. I recall seeing a very wealthy man in the first-class cabin who carried a walking stick that was encrusted with diamonds at the top. Since we departed Lagos, he had been getting up, pretending to go to the toilet every now and then to show everyone his expensive walking stick. However, when he heard the captain's announcement, he really needed to use the toilet.

I tell you with confidence that even if you are anointed, you will become frightened if you are told that your plane cannot land. Therefore, I turned to God and said, "Daddy, I embarked on this journey to do Your work. You didn't tell me when I was leaving to say goodbye to my family that it would be the last time I would see them." Then He replied, saying, "Don't worry, son. I'm only delaying the plane's landing because as soon as you land, people will not let you rest, and I need to talk to you first." God's word brought peace to my heart, and the plane continued to circle around the airport while God was speaking to me. When He finished talking to me, the faulty door opened, and the plane was able to make a normal landing. Despite how tough the situation was, I was at peace because God had spoken to me.

Beloved, when you have an intimate relationship with the Prince of Peace, you will not be troubled by the things that trouble others. You will not run helter-skelter at the hint of trouble because His word will bring peace to your heart. No matter how terrible a situation may be, there is always peace to be found in God's word. Turn to His word in such instances, and it will keep your heart at peace while turning things around for the better.
prayerPoints: Reflection: Do you have an intimate relationship with the Prince of Peace?
rccg_open_heavens.hymn: When Peace Like A River Attendeth My Way

rccg_rccg_ss_adult.title: Sanctification
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.author: RCCG Sunday School Directorate
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.memoryVerseText: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
message:
A. The apostle Paul, while addressing the Church in Corinth on God’s Standard of righteousness, emphasised that it is through sanctification that they are qualified to inherit God’s Kingdom. He started by asking:
Know ye not? ………………………………. Vs. 9a.
B. He further identified some of the unrighteous that will not inherit God’s kingdom, namely: ………………………… Vs. 9b-10.

i. Such were some………………………. vs.11a.

rccg_rccg_ss_adult.hymn: O Sunday School, on the Lord’s day
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.assignments: List five (5) practical ways a believer can daily live a sanctified life (2×5=10 marks).
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.introduction: Sanctification is a spiritual surgery performed by God in the life of a saved soul (Ezekiel 36:26). It is the second work of grace after salvation. Sanctification simply means to make holy, pure and separated unto God (Jeremiah 1:4-5). It is a progressive work of God in man that makes us free from sin and be like Christ (1 Thessalonians 5:23; Romans 8:13). It is vital to understand the process and benefits of sanctification.
outlines: THE PROCESS
THE BENEFITS
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.discussion:
1. THE PROCESS

A. To be sanctified

You need to see yourself as you are: filthy and in need of help
Cry to God for deliverance (Isaiah 6:5).
Present yourself to the Sanctifier – God (1 Thessalonians 5:23).
Surrender your heart to the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:2; 2 Thessalonians 2:13).
Study the word of God (John 17:17).
Soak yourself in the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 9:13-14; 1 John 1:7, 9).
Daily surrender to God (Colossians 3:6-10; Romans 6:13).
B. This process can be a painful experience, but:

The result is that you are broken and transformed into a new nature (Galatians 2:20; 2 Timothy 2:3-4).
The awareness that you do not own yourself anymore helps you prioritise God in everything you do, and whatever does not glorify Him is a no-go area for you (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
CLASS ACTIVITY 1: How do we avoid things that defile His Temple?

2. THE BENEFITS

Sanctification represents a believer’s victory over the flesh (Romans 7:24-25), the world (1 John 5:4), and the devil (James 4:7).
A sanctified believer will enjoy the ability to easily resist temptation because there is a renewed hatred for sin and lust.
Sanctification fosters intimacy with God, increases spiritual strength and stability (Psalm 15:1-5).
It also aids a ‘clean record’ for believers, that is, the enemy will not have to fool God over such (John 14:30).
It helps believers to be humble and submissive to God and to constituted authorities. The Adamic nature in man is subdued (Romans 8:1-5).
It gives the believer control over self (Galatians 2:20; Romans 6:13).
It promotes right standing before God and pure intentions of actions and words (Acts 24:16).
CLASS ACTIVITY 2: The class should discuss the ways sanctification helps a believer to live a life that honours God.
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.summary:
CONCLUSION: Sanctification is an integral part of Christian growth; every child of God must earnestly desire it.

EVALUATION: Briefly explain the process of sanctification.

CLOSING PRAYER: Father, I receive the grace to continually yield myself to your sanctification process in Jesus’ name.

dclm_dclm.title: Avoid Costly Mistakes
dclm_dclm.author: Pastor W.F. Kumuyi
dclm_dclm.memoryVerseText: Therefore, O Aholibah, thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will raise up thy lovers against thee, from whom thy mind is alienated, and I will bring them against thee on every side
message: Many times, what gets people into trouble are not big but little things. They omit to do what is right. They indulge in little careless or reckless acts, including those they knew spelt disaster for other people. With the passage of time, they become self confident in their ability to tackle issues their own way. They dismiss pointers in their own lives to things that caused misfortune for others on the hollow belief that ‘it cannot happen to me’. In the process, they seal their own misfortune.

Aholibah, or Judah in Israel, had witnessed judgement that came on Samaria (or Aholah) for turning away from God and embracing the nations that did not know the Lord. They were shipped into exile. Instead of learning from God’s retribution on evil nations, Judah became more sinful before God. They connived, formed alliances with heathen nations, exposed their treasure to them and served their idols. God paid them in their own coins: He turned their new friends against them, who plundered their wealth and exposed them to shame, humiliation and disgrace.

It is only reasonable to learn from the mistakes of other people and avoid things that brought them down. Where we find that the pursuit of power, wealth and pleasure took them away from God, we must flee from such. The lives of those around us who fell out with God should be a lesson to us to shun their ways. Anything that will lull our minds and dull our sensitivity to sinful enjoyment must be avoided. We must not wait to taste the judgment of God. Anything we must do to live right before God and avoid His rod of punishment must be done now. Mercifully, God gives us grace to live the acceptable life before Him. It is thus up to us to fully tap into that inexhaustible grace and present a commendable portrait of glory and beauty, rooted in His love.
dclm_dclm.thoughtForTheDay: Sin is deceptive and deadly, and those that toy with it have bitter tales to tell.

mfm_mfm.title: Jesus: The Master Over Every Storm
mfm_mfm.author: Dr. D.K. Olukoya
mfm_mfm.topic: Jesus: The Master Over Every Storm
mfm_mfm.memoryVerseText: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
message: When Jesus and His disciples were on the sea, and there was a storm, and His disciples shouted, “Master, Master, we are perishing,” I like the way Jesus rebuked them after calming the storm. What an insult! The One who, by the words of His mouth, commanded the same sea and the storm into existence, and can, by the blast of His nostrils, dry up both, was in the boat with them, and they were afraid? In the first instance, as we see in Luke 8:22, He was the One who said they should get into the boat and go over to the other side of the lake.

I have a number of questions for you to answer: Did you seek God’s face before you got into that marriage, or that business deal, or that job, or that ministry, or conceived that child? My friend, it is inevitable that there will be a few setbacks in your life because they are your stepping stones to success. Storms of life are the fire which your Creator uses to fine-tune your life and anchor you to Him, the Eternal Rock of Ages.

What then can the storm be? Is it barrenness in marriage? Is it failure in business? Is it problems in your ministry? Is it infirmity, sickness or disease? Ask Abraham, Elijah, the woman with the issue of blood, Peter, and so on. They had all been through storms, and the only thing that kept them going was their faith and obedience to God.

As in the case of the disciples on the sea, if He has led you into any situation, and a storm arises, He will never leave you nor forsake you. In fact, be of good cheer because He has overcome the world. This is why you must always carry Him along in whatever you do. In fact, NEVER enter a marriage or take any important decision in life without first knowing His will.

Beloved, do a regular audit of your heart and lifestyle to ensure that you are on course. If Jesus is asleep in the boat of your life, He says: “Peace, be still.” Also, ensure that you are always in praise mode. Then rejoice; the Lord is King.
mfm_mfm.motivationalQuote: Jehovah saw Elijah through all the threats of Jezebel. He will see you through all the rage from the pit of hell.

christ_embassy_rhapsody.title: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
christ_embassy_rhapsody.author: Pastor Chris Oyakhilome
christ_embassy_rhapsody.topic: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
christ_embassy_rhapsody.memoryVerseText: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…
message: 1 Peter 1:23 tells us something remarkable; it says, “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” A similar truth is emphasized in James 1:18, “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” God’s Word gave birth to you; and what does that make you?

It means you’re the Word in flesh! The Word of God is your life-source, and every living thing must be connected to its source to live. This is why your fellowship with the Word is so important. Your true life and environment are in the Word. If you live outside the Word, you’re functioning outside your divine environment.

The Apostle Paul, by the Spirit, connects and unveils this beautifully in 2 Corinthians 3:2-3. First, he says, “Ye are our epistle…” and then he goes further to say, “…ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…” You’re the living epistle, the living message, the living expression of Christ to your world. The Lord Jesus is called the living Word; therefore, being born of His Word, you carry His life, nature, wisdom and character within you.

You’re indestructible because you’re born of His indestructible seed (His Word), which lives and abides forever. Therefore, your sufficiency, your ability, competence, strength and capacity come from your divine origin. Many struggle in life because they don’t live according to this truth. They attempt to live outside the environment of the Word.

But the Christian who meditates on the Word continually stays connected to the source of his divine nature. The more the Word dominates your spirit, the more your true nature is unveiled. God’s Word created the universe. His Word is everything. As you meditate on it, it transforms your life. Think, speak, and live the Word. Glory to God!

rccg_ss_teacher_rccg_ss_teacher.memoryVerseText: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ
message: Sanctification
rccg_ss_teacher_rccg_ss_teacher.introduction: Sanctification is a spiritual surgery performed by God in the life of a saved soul (Ezekiel 36:26). It is the second work of grace after salvation. Sanctification simply means to make holy, pure and separated unto God (Jeremiah 1:4-5). It is a progressive work of God in man that makes us free from sin and be like Christ (1 Thessalonians 5:23; Romans 8:13). It is vital to understand the process and benefits of sanctification.

rhapsody.title: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
rhapsody.author: Pastor Chris Oyakhilome
rhapsody.topic: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
rhapsody.memoryVerseText: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…
message: 1 Peter 1:23 tells us something remarkable; it says, “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” A similar truth is emphasized in James 1:18, “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” God’s Word gave birth to you; and what does that make you?

It means you’re the Word in flesh! The Word of God is your life-source, and every living thing must be connected to its source to live. This is why your fellowship with the Word is so important. Your true life and environment are in the Word. If you live outside the Word, you’re functioning outside your divine environment.

The Apostle Paul, by the Spirit, connects and unveils this beautifully in 2 Corinthians 3:2-3. First, he says, “Ye are our epistle…” and then he goes further to say, “…ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…” You’re the living epistle, the living message, the living expression of Christ to your world. The Lord Jesus is called the living Word; therefore, being born of His Word, you carry His life, nature, wisdom and character within you.

You’re indestructible because you’re born of His indestructible seed (His Word), which lives and abides forever. Therefore, your sufficiency, your ability, competence, strength and capacity come from your divine origin. Many struggle in life because they don’t live according to this truth. They attempt to live outside the environment of the Word.

But the Christian who meditates on the Word continually stays connected to the source of his divine nature. The more the Word dominates your spirit, the more your true nature is unveiled. God’s Word created the universe. His Word is everything. As you meditate on it, it transforms your life. Think, speak, and live the Word. Glory to God!
rhapsody.hymn: I’m born of God’s incorruptible Word; I’m the living epistle of Christ. My life is the manifestation of divine wisdom, glory and power. As I meditate on the Word, even now, I’m strengthened, transformed and established in victory, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

dunamis_seeds.title: A Heart For The Kingdom
dunamis_seeds.author: Pastor Dr. Paul Enenche
dunamis_seeds.memoryVerseText: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
message: Our anchor Scripture makes it clear that your heart follows your investment. That is why you cannot claim to love the Kingdom while your resources are committed elsewhere.

The Roman centurion demonstrated this scriptural truth in Luke Chapter Seven.
Concerning him the elders of the Jews testified to Jesus, “for he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue” (Luke 7:5). You see, a heart for the Kingdom was what changed his story; it was what made Jesus to come.

Investment into the Kingdom contributes to man’s fulfilment on earth. Your seed into the Kingdom will reply to your needs when they arise. But there are people who have no seed to reply to the needs of their lives. When you are seedless, when your needs come up, nothing can help you. To be seedless is to be fruitless.

When the purpose of God does not interest you, the problems of your life will never attract Him. There are people going to church for years, yet they have never sacrificed anything for the Kingdom. When the offering basket is being passed around them, they just watch it pass by them to the next person. When it is time to build the church, to plant other churches, to send people on evangelism, to invest in television evangelism, or to even pay tithe; they look away. Yet when their problems arrive, they want God to help them. God seems to be saying: “You are not interested in Me, so I am not attracted to you. “Draw near to me, I will draw near to you” (James 4:6-7).
Don’t sit in church expecting a heavenly bank to credit you where you have made no deposit; God is your heavenly Father, not merely a source to withdraw from.

When was the last time you did something for God that touched you? Where you sow your seed will determine where you get your harvest. He that soweth to the flesh, from the flesh he will reap frustration, (Galatians 6:8) because he is spending all on what to eat, drink, wear, and drive. He that soweth to the spirit – so that churches can be built and the devil chased back to hell, will reap satisfaction. It is a matter of choice.

I came to a point in my life where I decided I would not spend anything on myself that I had not first given to God. I have been hard on myself but liberal toward the Kingdom, giving amounts I could have used to buy cars, not once, not twice. And the truth is, I do not need to spend money on hospital bills or fighting witchcraft attacks, because I have already seeded into the Kingdom, and the Kingdom attacks the need at its root.

Beloved, the Kingdom is not about what you have; it is about what you have released. Every seed planted into the things of God is a need already answered, and a battle already fought and won before it even arises.
prayerPoints: Examine what you have genuinely sacrificed for the Kingdom lately.
Correct any area of seedlessness in your life.
Choose one Kingdom project, evangelism, church building, or missions, and sow into it this week.
Draw near to God through consistent giving and service, not merely attendance.

PRAYER: Father, forgive me for every form of seedless existence. Give me a heart that is liberal toward Your Kingdom. Let my seed answer my need before it arises and let my life bring You the fulfilment You desire, Lord, in Jesus’ Name.

QUOTE: Show me a man who does not care about the cause of God on the earth, and I will show you a God who also does not care about such a man. Culled from the book 30 Secrets to the Top by Dr Paul Enenche

rccg_open_heavens.title: THE BREATH OF GOD
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: Thus saith the Lord God unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live:
message: In John 20:19-22, the Bible tells us that when Jesus visited His disciples, He breathed on them. When God visits a person, He breathes on him or her. Adam was a lifeless lump of clay until God breathed on him in Genesis 2:7. When the breath of God went into him, he became a living being. The once lifeless creature came alive and began to walk around, talk, and even name animals. A person will remain ordinary until God breathes life into him or her. Likewise, the breath of God on a lifeless project will bring it to life, and it will eventually become successful. I pray in the name that is above every other name that God will breathe upon you and all that concerns you.

In Ezekiel 37:1-10, the Bible tells us that Prophet Ezekiel found himself in the middle of a valley that was full of bones. The bones were not just many, they were also very dry and lifeless. They would have continued experiencing dryness and death if God had not intervened. He sent His word through the prophet and breathed upon them. As soon as the breath of the Almighty God came upon them, they came together, flesh and sinews came upon them, and they arose as a great army. The bones that had previously looked dry and powerless now became a mighty and formidable force because of the breath of God. I decree that every dry or dead situation in your life will begin to live again henceforth, in Jesus' name.

Many people have visions of something great they want to achieve, and even though they have tried to pursue those visions, things have not gone as they expected. As a result, many of those visions have been abandoned and forgotten. Today's Bible reading tells us that when the Israelites returned to Jerusalem to build the temple in Zerubbabel's time, they faced opposition from their neighbours, and at one point they even had to put the construction on hold (Ezra 4:24). The situation remained the same until God sent His prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, to prophesy to the people. Their prophecy released the breath of God upon them, and the work that had been halted resumed and was completed successfully.   Beloved, I decree that God will breathe into your life, family, career, visions, and all that concerns you, in Jesus' name.
prayerPoints: God's breath releases a new lease of life into everything it enters.
rccg_open_heavens.hymn: Pass Me Not, O Gentle Saviour

rccg_open_heavens.title: YOU HAVE A PURPOSE
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
message: After Jesus resurrected from the dead, He visited His disciples in John 20:19-22 and said to them, "...as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you." When God comes into a person's life, He will give the person a purpose for his or her life. He will share His thoughts and plans with the person and show him or her what the future holds. He will do this because He desires His children to live purposeful lives.

Many people are drifting through life because they haven't encountered Jesus. They do anything that appeals to them because they have not discovered why God created them. For instance, some of them engage in fraudulent acts just to make money. At the end of the day, they realise that life is more than having money. Such people become rich but miserable because the wealth they amassed, which they thought would bring them joy and fulfilment, did not. They soon discover that their lives lack meaning despite their wealth. They do not know God's purpose for their lives, so they continually strive to achieve the next big thing. Unfortunately, after each seemingly big achievement, they tend to sink into despair because they feel as if something is still missing in their lives.

Child of God, no amount of money, fame, or achievement can make a person fulfilled. As long as a person lives outside God's purpose for his or her life, such a person will not know what true fulfilment is. I have had the opportunity to mingle with the high and mighty, and I have discovered that some people who are poor by societal definitions have more joy and peace than many. In today's memory verse, the Almighty God says that He knows the plans He has towards you, and that they are good.

Beloved, God has a specific plan for your life, and it is only when you align yourself with His plan that you will experience fulfilment. To know His purpose for your life, you must cultivate an intimate relationship with Him because He created you, and no product can fulfil its true purpose outside its manufacturer's intention and specifications. As you spend quality time with your Maker in prayer and studying His word, your true purpose will become evident. I pray that God will continually guide you along the path of your purpose in Him and supply you with the grace and wisdom to fulfil it, in Jesus' name.
prayerPoints: Do you know God's purpose for your life, and are you walking in it?

rccg_open_heavens.title: PRAYERS FOR YOUR NATION
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people.
message:
1.	Father, I thank You for my nation. Thank You for Your mighty hand of power that has sustained us over the years. 
2.	Father, please have mercy on my nation. Let Your abundant mercy preserve us from evil, in Jesus' name. 
3.	Father, please put godly men and women in leadership positions. Please Lord, let Your will be done in this nation, in Jesus' name. 
4.	Father, please let Your wisdom guide the hearts of our leaders and those in authority. Give them the grace to lead us right, in Jesus' name. 
5.	Lord, please arrest the hearts of kidnappers, ritualists, oppressors, and other evil people in my nation. Let them not know peace until they turn from their wicked ways and surrender to You, in Jesus' name. 
6.	Father, please let every aspect of my nation's economy thrive and prosper. Cause the breath of Your peace and grace to blow across every sector, in Jesus' name. 
7.	Father, please let the positive prophecies that have been spoken over my nation come to pass. Please establish Your word concerning this nation, in Jesus' name. 
8.	Father, please let Your light shine over my nation. Let every form of confusion and stagnation come to an end, and let Your light bring stability and progress, in Jesus' name. 
9.	Father, please let there be peace in my nation. Remove tribalism, strife, racism, and all forms of darkness that turn people against one another, in Jesus' name. 
10.	Father, please strengthen and guide our youths. Let our youths rise to take their rightful place in every sector of the economy. Let them not get carried away with youthful lusts, in Jesus' name. 
11.	Father, please destroy every plan of the devil to plunge my nation into sorrow. Let Your joy fill this land, and make us fruitful in all areas, in Jesus' name. 
12.	Your personal prayer points for your nation.

mfm.title: Pray For Your Country
mfm.author: Dr. D.K. Olukoya
mfm.memoryVerseText: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
message: the inhabitants thereof for His purpose and glory. All the glorious plans of God for every nation can only become a reality as the nations and her citizens submit to the will of God and exalt righteous living above vicious existence. That is the reason why the Scripture says, “Righteousness exalts a nation but sin is a reproach to any people” (Proverbs 14:34),

dunamis_seeds.title: The Practice Of Love
dunamis_seeds.author: Pastor Dr. Paul Enenche
dunamis_seeds.memoryVerseText: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal… Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil.
message: Our anchor Scripture emphasizes the importance of love above all other virtues. It makes four things critically clear:

1.	Speaking in tongues equals noise without love. Lovelessness drowns the voice of prayer. Hatred or unforgiveness in the heart drowns a person’s voice at the place of prayer. If you do not love your brother, sister, or neighbour, you are wasting your time at the place of prayer.

2.	Insight from Scripture is a waste without love. Revelation cannot guarantee any meaningful outcome in the absence of love. Where love is absent, revelation means nothing; insight means nothing. That is why there are many people whose heads are filled with Scripture, but their lives are empty of results. It doesn’t matter what you know; until you know love, you know nothing.

3.	Faith is fake without love, because faith worketh by love (Galatians 5:6). Many people say, “I believe, I have faith,” while there is bitterness in their heart towards someone, and still wonder why they are not seeing results.

4.	Giving is unprofitable without love. Even giving one’s body to be burned for the sake of the gospel profits nothing without love.
Giving without love equals sowing without reaping; such giving is not permitted to yield the expected harvest. 1 Corinthians 13:3If prayer is useless without love, if revelation is a waste without love, if faith cannot work without love, and if sowing is useless without love, then nothing we do is meaningful and profitable without love.
Now, what is the practicality of love? We shall be looking at a few of them in our study today.

1.	Love is very patient (1 Corinthians 13:4).
Love is both tolerant and tireless. It has a large capacity to accommodate human error. Living with a spouse requires this kind of patience

2.	Love is kind (1 Corinthians 13:4).
Love is liberal; love is not tight-fisted or stingy. A man who is tight-fisted toward his wife, children, and other loved ones is operating outside the vocabulary of love.

3.	Love does not envy (1 Corinthians 13:4).
When you love people, you don’t compete with them; you commend their effort. Love does not struggle to outdo, undo, or diminish others; it struggles only to give honest expression to what God has placed within, not to create impressions.
Beloved, love is life. Walk in love, because love affects life, both in time and in eternity. Love guarantees profitability and productivity for our spirituality. Our prayer life, giving, faith, and insight are all at the mercy of our love walk.
prayerPoints: Father, let love be the foundation of everything I do, so that none of my effort is wasted. Teach me to be patient, kind, and give me the grace to make amends where necessary, Lord, in Jesus’ Name.
dunamis_seeds.thoughtForTheDay: It doesn’t matter what you know; until you know love, you know nothing.

rccg_open_heavens.title: REMAIN GRATEFUL
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works.
message: Sometime ago, I went to a man's house to conduct a programme. It was a night programme, and the owner of the house asked me to spend the night at his house afterwards because it was too late for me to return home. I obliged, and in the morning, he asked me to wait for breakfast. When it was time to eat, a chef came and asked my host what he wanted to eat. After so much back and forth, my host finally decided that he would have bread and eggs for breakfast. Then, for the next few minutes, another back-and-forth ensued because the chef asked my host how he wanted his eggs prepared - scrambled, poached, or fried - before he finally settled on boiled eggs. Then, it was time for another debate: how do you want your egg boiled, hard-boiled or medium-boiled? By then, it had been more than 25 minutes, and I had gotten really hungry. Finally, the chef turned to me when he finished with his boss and asked, "Sir, what will you eat?" I told him to give me anything he had. He said he had bread and eggs, and I said it was fine. Then, he asked if I wanted an omelette or bacon, the number of eggs I wanted, and so on. I told him that anything was fine, as long as it was enough to satisfy my hunger. After the whole ordeal, I thought to myself that even though I had no money, I had a good appetite at least. Child of God, while you may not have everything you desire in life yet, you must be grateful for the things you have.

Ecclesiastes 6:9 says that the sight of the eyes is better than the wandering of desire. Many people are not grateful for what they have because they are consumed with thinking about the things they want. They do not appreciate the things they can see because of their wandering desires. Beloved, if God has given you the gift of life, be grateful. Ecclesiastes 9:4 says that as long as you are joined to all the living, there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion. As long as you are alive, there is hope that you will achieve the things you desire. Don't be so focused on the things you wish you had that you forget to appreciate God for all you already have. In all things, give thanks (1 Thessalonians 5:18).
prayerPoints: Reflection:  Are you grateful for the things you have?

sunday_school_lessons.memoryVerseText: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
message:
A. The apostle Paul, while addressing the Church in Corinth on God’s Standard of righteousness, emphasised that it is through sanctification that they are qualified to inherit God’s Kingdom. He started by asking:
Know ye not? ………………………………. Vs. 9a.
B. He further identified some of the unrighteous that will not inherit God’s kingdom, namely: ………………………… Vs. 9b-10.

i. Such were some………………………. vs.11a.
ii. But ………………………….. Vs. 11b.
sunday_school_lessons.hymn: O Sunday School, on the Lord’s day
sunday_school_lessons.assignments: List five (5) practical ways a believer can daily live a sanctified life (2×5=10 marks).
sunday_school_lessons.introduction: Sanctification is a spiritual surgery performed by God in the life of a saved soul (Ezekiel 36:26). It is the second work of grace after salvation. Sanctification simply means to make holy, pure and separated unto God (Jeremiah 1:4-5). It is a progressive work of God in man that makes us free from sin and be like Christ (1 Thessalonians 5:23; Romans 8:13). It is vital to understand the process and benefits of sanctification.
outlines: THE PROCESS
THE BENEFITS
sunday_school_lessons.discussion:
1. THE PROCESS

A. To be sanctified

You need to see yourself as you are: filthy and in need of help
Cry to God for deliverance (Isaiah 6:5).
Present yourself to the Sanctifier – God (1 Thessalonians 5:23).
Surrender your heart to the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:2; 2 Thessalonians 2:13).
Study the word of God (John 17:17).
Soak yourself in the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 9:13-14; 1 John 1:7, 9).
Daily surrender to God (Colossians 3:6-10; Romans 6:13).
B. This process can be a painful experience, but:

The result is that you are broken and transformed into a new nature (Galatians 2:20; 2 Timothy 2:3-4).
The awareness that you do not own yourself anymore helps you prioritise God in everything you do, and whatever does not glorify Him is a no-go area for you (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
CLASS ACTIVITY 1: How do we avoid things that defile His Temple?

2. THE BENEFITS

Sanctification represents a believer’s victory over the flesh (Romans 7:24-25), the world (1 John 5:4), and the devil (James 4:7).
A sanctified believer will enjoy the ability to easily resist temptation because there is a renewed hatred for sin and lust.
Sanctification fosters intimacy with God, increases spiritual strength and stability (Psalm 15:1-5).
It also aids a ‘clean record’ for believers, that is, the enemy will not have to fool God over such (John 14:30).
It helps believers to be humble and submissive to God and to constituted authorities. The Adamic nature in man is subdued (Romans 8:1-5).
It gives the believer control over self (Galatians 2:20; Romans 6:13).
It promotes right standing before God and pure intentions of actions and words (Acts 24:16).
CLASS ACTIVITY 2: The class should discuss the ways sanctification helps a believer to live a life that honours God.
sunday_school_lessons.summary:
CONCLUSION: Sanctification is an integral part of Christian growth; every child of God must earnestly desire it.

EVALUATION: Briefly explain the process of sanctification.

CLOSING PRAYER: Father, I receive the grace to continually yield myself to your sanctification process in Jesus’ name.

sunday_school_lessons.title: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
sunday_school_lessons.author: Pastor Chris Oyakhilome
sunday_school_lessons.topic: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
sunday_school_lessons.memoryVerseText: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…
message: 1 Peter 1:23 tells us something remarkable; it says, “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” A similar truth is emphasized in James 1:18, “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” God’s Word gave birth to you; and what does that make you?

It means you’re the Word in flesh! The Word of God is your life-source, and every living thing must be connected to its source to live. This is why your fellowship with the Word is so important. Your true life and environment are in the Word. If you live outside the Word, you’re functioning outside your divine environment.

The Apostle Paul, by the Spirit, connects and unveils this beautifully in 2 Corinthians 3:2-3. First, he says, “Ye are our epistle…” and then he goes further to say, “…ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…” You’re the living epistle, the living message, the living expression of Christ to your world. The Lord Jesus is called the living Word; therefore, being born of His Word, you carry His life, nature, wisdom and character within you.

You’re indestructible because you’re born of His indestructible seed (His Word), which lives and abides forever. Therefore, your sufficiency, your ability, competence, strength and capacity come from your divine origin. Many struggle in life because they don’t live according to this truth. They attempt to live outside the environment of the Word.

But the Christian who meditates on the Word continually stays connected to the source of his divine nature. The more the Word dominates your spirit, the more your true nature is unveiled. God’s Word created the universe. His Word is everything. As you meditate on it, it transforms your life. Think, speak, and live the Word. Glory to God!
sunday_school_lessons.hymn: I’m born of God’s incorruptible Word; I’m the living epistle of Christ. My life is the manifestation of divine wisdom, glory and power. As I meditate on the Word, even now, I’m strengthened, transformed and established in victory, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
